english.title: Disclose information about a prisoner in a secure training centre

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: CRIMINAL JUSTICE AND PUBLIC ORDER ACT 1994

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..)

(A)_[being employed]_
(B)_[having been employed]_

(C)_[in pursuance of escort arrangements]_
(D)_[at a contracted out secure training centre]_
(E)_[to perform contracted out functions at a directly managed secure training centre]_

disclosed, otherwise than in the course of your duty or as authorised by the Secretary of State, information, namely **(..SPECIFY INFORMATION..), which you acquired in the course of your employment and which related to **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), an offender detained at a secure training centre
english.legislation: Contrary to section 14(1) and (2) of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: See section 15 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994 for definitions.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
